thread:
jordan: heads-up — we're seeing steady memory growth on long streaming chat sessions on canary. KV residency climbs ~1.7GB over ~6h for a few sessions. suspicious.
lee: can you share the rough repro? workload shape / batch sizes / model? @tara FYI
jordan: it's the usual longtool loop + interactive streaming (many small assistant turns). batch size ~16, avg seq 120, occasional 2k spikes. model variant = redwood/opt-grp-13b-int8. happens only when sessions stay open and tool loops hit multiple rerank cycles.
tara: ok. i pulled a flamegraph from the run: most time is still token gen but memory PSS keeps increasing. kv stats attached from agent (snip):
```
KV_STAT pages_total=12540 pages_resident=8200 pages_pinned=180
KV_STAT resident_bytes=7_300_000_000 reclaimable=1_720_000_000
HEAP rss=9_120_000_000 committed=8_450_000_000
```
mike: interesting — reclaimable stays high but not reclaimed. indicates fragmentation or pinned pages. did you see refcounts not dropping?
jordan: heapmaps show a growing number of small live allocations tied to kv slabs. profiler points to pagewalk + refcount bump hotspots during toolloop exit.
tara: i ran a quick heap diff; a lot of entries are KV-era small 'prefix' entries around 256-1024 bytes that never age out because toolloop reuses prefixes with slightly different keys. fragmentation -> slab inefficiency.
lee: could be our eviction heuristic; we favor LRU but prefixes with similar keys get reinserts that keep them 'young'. also batching heuristics cause many tiny writes in quick succession which prevents clean eviction windows.
mike: quick experiment: reduce max_live_prefixes and force compaction every N minutes in canary. command i used locally:
```
./bin/serve --kv-max-prefixes=20000 --kv-forced-compaction-interval=300 --log-level=debug
```
jordan: ran that overnight — reduced steady-state growth to ~400MB over same period. but saw a perf hit at compaction time (~60-120ms p99 latency spike) :/ 
ci-bot: deploy pipeline succeeded for canary with kv-forced-compaction-interval=300 (build 2026.03.17-canary)
lee: tradeoff. maybe we can make compaction incremental to avoid big p99 blips. tara, can you capture a trace during compaction window (perf + heap) and paste the short traces?
tara: pasted short trace gist: https://redwood-gists/internal/abc123
tara: trace shows compaction work dominated by page coalesce and memmove; allocator churn spikes. suspect slab size classes mismatch — many small allocations live in mid-size slab buckets.
mike: proposal: add an adaptive compaction that triggers only when reclaimable/resident > threshold AND average prefix reuse < X. and make compaction incremental (batch of pages per cycle).
jordan: agree. also we should look at batching heuristics: grouping small writes into micro-batches could reduce churn.
lee: i'll open an issue with action items: reproduce script, perf traces, compaction patch, and a short experiment plan. assign to eng-runtime + perf. tags: kv, compaction, longstream, regression.
mike: note — kernel selection for int8 path cropping looked unrelated in the profile; no heavy kernel changes concurrent with growth. putting that aside.
tara: for immediate mitigation we can enable forced incremental compaction on canary and lower kv-max-prefixes. i'll add a PR with config flags.
jordan: thanks. next steps: 1) lee opens issue + checklist, 2) tara lands incremental compaction experiment, 3) mike runs micro-batching experiment, 4) monitor canary p99 and mem-residency for 48h. ping me on thread with links. :thumbsup:
lee: done — https://redwood-issues/ENG-5129
mike: i'll run micro-batching tonight and report numbers tomorrow.
